Profile likelihood inference

Source: R/firth-profile.R
fastglm_profile_test.Rd

Tests one or more coefficient values by comparing an unrestricted maximum with the maximum under those constraints. The remaining coefficients are re-estimated. Binomial-logit Firth fits use their penalized likelihood; ordinal maximum-likelihood fits use their ordinary likelihood. For intervals, use confint(object, method = "profile"); the default confint() method remains Wald inference.

fastglm_profile_test(object, parm, null = 0, control = list(), contrast = NULL)

Arguments

object

a converged binomial-logit Firth model or an ordinal maximum-likelihood model, with a retained dense design matrix and response and a full-rank design. Ordinal models require every category to be observed.

parm

coefficient names or indices. The test treats all selected coefficients jointly; confidence intervals profile each separately. Omit parm when supplying an ordinal contrast matrix.

null

hypothesized coefficient values, in the order specified by parm, or one value per row of contrast. A scalar is repeated.

control

named list of numerical controls: maxit = 300 limits each nuisance optimization; reltol = 1e-12 is its objective tolerance; score.tol = 1e-5 bounds the adjusted score after scaling by coefficient standard errors; root.tol = 1e-6 is the endpoint tolerance in these same standardized units; max.expand = 25 limits bracket expansions; and max.root = 100 limits root iterations. Ordinal controls are described in fastglm_score_test().

contrast

optional numeric vector or full-row-rank numeric matrix for ordinal tests. Columns correspond to the full coefficient vector; names may select a subset. Each matrix row specifies a linear hypothesis. For example, differences between a predictor's threshold-specific slopes test whether that predictor has a common effect while other effects remain unrestricted.

Value

fastglm_profile_test() returns a fastglm_test object inheriting from htest, with a compact printed table and as.data.frame() and optional broom::tidy() extraction. It retains the statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, coefficient estimates, hypothesized values, the full and constrained log likelihoods (penalized for Firth fits, excluding constants independent of coefficients), and diagnostics containing convergence, scaled scores, optimizer codes, evaluation counts, and messages. confint(..., method = "profile") returns a two-column fastglm_confint matrix with diagnostics, fit.diagnostics, and method attributes. Each diagnostic row identifies the coefficient and endpoint, convergence, likelihood-ratio statistic and target, root error, scaled nuisance score, optimizer code, and failure message.

Details

For binomial-logit Firth models the objective is the binomial log likelihood plus one half of the log determinant of the full Fisher information matrix. Tested columns remain in that determinant when their coefficients are constrained. Grouped binomial responses, frequency weights, and offsets retain their fitted meanings. Effective successes and failures must be nonnegative integer counts, allowing arithmetic round-off. Fractional power or survey weights are unsupported. Zero-weight observations make no contribution.

For ordinal maximum-likelihood fits, the objective is the joint cumulative-link log likelihood, including partial proportional-odds and other nonparallel cumulative-link models. Thresholds and untested slopes are re-estimated subject to the selected coefficient constraints. Logit, probit, and complementary log-log links, grouped category counts, frequency weights, and offsets retain their fitted meanings. Ordinal mean bias reduction does not generally maximize a penalized likelihood and is unsupported by this profile method; fastglm_score_test() provides an analytic score procedure with an explicit null-estimation convention.

The likelihood-ratio statistic uses an asymptotic chi-square reference with one degree of freedom per constraint. Profile intervals invert its one-parameter version. These are approximations under an independent binomial or ordinal sampling model, including frequency-weighted observations; they are not exact finite-sample or cluster-robust procedures.

Sparse, mapped, and streaming designs are currently unsupported rather than converted to dense matrices. Native evaluation uses additional memory of order the squared number of coefficients plus a fixed block of rows. Ordinal constrained inference also creates a standardized dense design, requiring additional storage proportional to observations times predictors; it does not construct an observation-by-category-by-parameter array.

Every constrained optimization checks the ordinary or adjusted score of the free coefficients. The unrestricted fit is checked and refined when needed. Failed tests return missing statistics and p-values with a warning; failed confidence limits are missing, with endpoint diagnostics attached. No Wald replacement is made. Optimization starts from the fitted solution; convergence diagnostics do not establish that a global maximum has been found in a multimodal problem.

References

Heinze, G. and Schemper, M. (2002). A solution to the problem of separation in logistic regression. Statistics in Medicine, 21, 2409–2419. doi:10.1002/sim.1047 .

Examples

d <- data.frame(y = rep(0:1, each = 10), x = rep(0:1, each = 10))
fit <- fastglm(y ~ x, d, family = binomial(), firth = TRUE)
confint(fit, parm = "x", method = "profile")
#> Profile confidence intervals
#> Method: Firth penalized profile likelihood
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#>   2.5 % 97.5 %
#> x 2.962  11.86
fastglm_profile_test(fit, parm = "x")
#> Firth penalized likelihood ratio test (asymptotic chi-square reference)
#> Null fit: Firth penalized likelihood
#> 
#>  Statistic df p-value
#>      22.36  1 < 1e-04
#> 
#> Tested coefficients:
#>   Estimate  Null
#> x    6.089 0.000
